# Phase B — build one replica

You build exactly one static website replica: the single approved source in your task, into the single directory the orchestrator writes for you. One run is one replica. Do not start a second site, do not change the source, and do not widen the page map. If the approved source, its page map or the model attribution in your task looks wrong or missing, stop and say so — that is a real blocker, not permission to choose for yourself.

The build runs over several exchanges. Emit files through the file protocol, end each reply with a status line, and the orchestrator writes what you send and tells you what it wrote. It also tells you when a file was rejected and why; fix and resend that file.

## Suggested order

1. **Plan.** No files yet. List the local pages from the approved map, the shared components each page uses, the sample datasets you will inline and their row counts, and the interactions you will implement. Keep it short.
2. **Shell.** `css/styles.css`, `js/main.js`, `index.html`. These three set the pattern every later page follows.
3. **Pages.** Two or three per reply, in the map's order, then `404.html`.
4. **Assets.** Local `.svg` placeholders as you need them.
5. **Documentation.** `README.md`, `fidelity-notes.md`, `component-inventory.json`, `generation-metadata.json`.

## Technology — the hard boundary

Semantic HTML5, standard CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript using browser-native APIs. One `css/styles.css` and one `js/main.js` shared by every page unless complexity genuinely demands a split.

Prohibited, without exception: React, Vue, Angular, Svelte and any other framework or component system; jQuery, Bootstrap, Tailwind, any CSS framework, UI kit or icon font; TypeScript, JSX, templating engines, npm packages, bundlers, any build step; PHP, Python, server-side includes, databases, APIs, authentication, backends; remote CDNs, web fonts loaded over the network, third-party widgets, trackers and embeds.

Every page must work by opening the file directly in a browser — `file://`, no server. So: relative paths only, never a root-absolute `/path`; no `fetch()` of local JSON, because browsers block it over `file://` — inline your demo data as JavaScript arrays or objects; all images local, `.svg` preferred. If any feature would need a local HTTP server, drop it rather than requiring one. `href="#"`, dead buttons and controls that silently do nothing are failures: every visible control either works on local data or is clearly labelled a non-functional demonstration.

## Fidelity and originality

Reproduce the reference's information architecture, layout patterns, hierarchy, navigation structure and interaction patterns. Do not reproduce its identity: use a fictional organization name, original prose, and original placeholder artwork. No real logos, wordmarks, seals, trademarks, copyrighted text, real photographs, real staff, real testimonials or real statistics. Nothing may claim a measured outcome or an endorsement.

Build only what the evidence in your task supports. The category checklist is conditional — omit a feature the reference does not have, and label anything you add on purpose as an intentional addition in the fidelity notes. No universal homepage template, no page-count quota, no hundreds of mock records: enough sample data to exercise filters, empty states, errors and keyboard flows, with the counts stated in the README.

Where the reference's flow depends on a real service — payment, ordering, reservation, application, login, portal, donation, subscription — implement a simulation with a clearly marked demo outcome, or an accessible non-functional demonstration with an explanation. Never imply that a transaction, submission or account action really happened. Follow your category's simulation restrictions exactly; some categories forbid plausible-looking content outright, such as live weather alerts or health advice.

## Accessibility baseline

Target WCAG 2.2 Level AA as an implementation standard. Every page needs: `<html lang>`; a skip link to `#main-content` that is the first focusable element and visible on focus; `<main id="main-content">` plus header, nav and footer landmarks; exactly one `<h1>` and a logical heading order with no skipped levels; native `<button>`, `<a>`, `<input>` and `<label>` in preference to ARIA, with ARIA only where native semantics fall short; programmatic labels on every field, with inline errors, an error summary, and focus moved to the problem; `aria-expanded` on disclosures and menus; Escape closing menus and dialogs, with focus returned to the trigger; a visible focus indicator everywhere; text alternatives that carry meaning, and `alt=""` on decorative art; sufficient contrast, and state never signalled by colour alone; responsive reflow with no horizontal scrolling at 375px; and `prefers-reduced-motion` respected.

Write that this is a WCAG-oriented baseline. Do not write that the site is compliant or conformant — no audit has happened. Do not introduce defects on purpose.

## Research instrumentation

Tag every meaningful region and reusable component instance with stable kebab-case attributes: `data-section` for the page region, `data-component` for the recognizable UI pattern, both where they apply. The same pattern keeps the same `data-component` value across pages and sites, for example `site-header`, `primary-nav`, `card-grid`, `contact-form`, `site-footer`. Add `data-instance` where one page holds several instances. Do not tag incidental spans. These are research metadata and never a substitute for semantic HTML or ARIA.

## Required documentation

- `README.md` — replica ID; category; fictional branding; the approved source URL; verification method and date exactly as the task states them; how to open the site locally; the full sitemap; the page-to-source mapping; sample dataset row counts; interaction and simulation notes; the seven QC gates of `Rules.md` section 9 reported as pass, fail or not tested; and what was not tested. Screen readers, zoom, manual keyboard walkthroughs and non-Chromium browsers are not tested unless the orchestrator tells you they were.
- `fidelity-notes.md` — page by page and component by component, what is replicated, approximated, simulated, intentionally added, omitted or unverified, with a reason for every material deviation, and anything worth knowing for the research.
- `component-inventory.json` — valid JSON in the `Rules.md` section 8 shape: every unique component with its selector, the pages it actually appears on, its behaviours, its keyboard expectations, and its real status and validation state.
- `generation-metadata.json` — valid JSON in the `MODEL_ALLOCATION.md` section 6 shape. Copy the identifiers, model attribution, approval and revision values from your task verbatim; they are recorded facts, not fields to fill from memory. Leave `validation_summary` gates at `not-tested` — the orchestrator sets them from the real QC run — and never copy another group's model IDs or dates.

## Finishing

Your last reply emits `=== STATUS: COMPLETE ===` and a short closing note: the fictional name, the page and file counts, the interactions you implemented, and every deviation and limitation you know of. Then stop. The orchestrator runs the shared QC and comes back if anything failed. Preparation is not delivery, QC passing is not acceptance, and acceptance is a human decision made elsewhere.


## The file protocol

Emit every file between sentinel lines, exactly like this:

=== FILE: index.html ===
<!doctype html>
...complete file contents...
=== END FILE ===

Rules for the protocol:
- One sentinel pair per file. Never nest them and never put two files in one block.
- Always write the file's COMPLETE contents. There is no patch or diff mode, and "..." or
  "unchanged" placeholders are rejected. Re-emitting a path replaces that file.
- Paths are relative to the site root and lowercase, except README.md, and limited to the site root or
  css/, js/, assets/ and data/. Allowed extensions: .html .css .js .svg .json .md .txt
- Markdown code fences inside a block are optional and are stripped if present.
- End every reply with one status line:
    === STATUS: CONTINUE ===   more files still to come, you will be asked to go on
    === STATUS: COMPLETE ===   the deliverable is finished
- If a reply would be cut off, stop at a file boundary, emit CONTINUE, and finish in the next reply.
- Prose outside the blocks is kept as your notes; keep it short.

Size limits: at most 120 files and 600 KB per file.

**Plan for replica HOSP-08**

**Local pages (build order)**  
1. index.html – home  
2. get-care-now.html – appointment inquiry  
3. pay-a-bill.html – billing/insurance  
4. find-a-doctor.html – provider listing (all specialties)  
5. find-a-doctor-primary-care.html – provider listing filtered to primary care  
6. health-care-services.html – services overview  
7. conditions-and-treatments.html – conditions detail listing  
8. location-map.html – interactive location map  
9. locations-hospitals.html – hospital locations list  
10. patient-resources.html – patient and visitor information  
11. 404.html – not‑found page  

**Shared components (selector → pages)**  
- `site-header` – all pages  
- `primary-nav` – all pages (contains links to home, get‑care‑now, pay‑a‑bill, find‑a‑doctor, services, locations, patient resources)  
- `skip-link` – first focusable element on every page  
- `hero-banner` – index.html only (large call‑to‑action)  
- `service-bands` – index.html and health-care-services.html (horizontal bands with icons/text)  
- `provider-listing-band` – find-a-doctor.html and find-a-doctor-primary-care.html (card grid of doctors)  
- `location-map-band` – location-map.html (static SVG map placeholder) and locations-hospitals.html (list of hospitals)  
- `site-footer` – all pages  
- `breadcrumb` – optional on interior pages (get-care-now, pay-a-bill, find-a-doctor*, health-care-services, conditions-and-treatments, location-map, locations-hospitals, patient-resources)  

**Inline sample datasets (row counts)**  
- `doctors.js` – array of 12 doctor objects (id, name, specialty, acceptingNewPatients, locationId)  
- `services.js` – array of 8 service objects (id, title, shortDescription, icon)  
- `locations.js` – array of 6 location objects (id, name, address, phone, hospitalId)  
- `hospitals.js` – array of 4 hospital objects (id, name, address, phone, website)  
- `insurancePlans.js` – array of 4 plan objects (id, name, networkTier)  
- `patientResources.js` – array of 5 resource objects (id, title, url, category)  

**Interactions to implement**  
- **Doctor filter** (observed_key_interactions: doctor filter) – client‑side filter on the provider‑listing band; users type a specialty or name, the doctor list updates; cleared via Escape.  
- **Location filter** (observed_key_interactions: location filter) – on location-map.html and locations-hospitals.html, a dropdown filters locations by city/zip; results update without page reload.  
- **Service navigation** (observed_key_interactions: service navigation) – service bands act as accordion tabs; clicking a band expands/collapses its description panel; keyboard operable (Enter/Space).  
- **Appointment‑request validation** (observed_key_interactions: appointment-request validation) – simple form on get-care-now.html with fields for name, email, phone, preferred date, reason; inline validation shows errors, error summary appears, focus moves to first invalid field on submit; submit shows a simulated confirmation modal (no real booking).  
- **Billing/insurance information** (observed_key_interactions: billing/insurance information) – on pay-a-bill.html, a button “View accepted insurance plans” opens a modal listing the insurancePlans dataset; modal is dismissible with Escape and returns focus to the button.  

**Items we cannot build and why**  
- Detailed doctor or service detail pages are absent from the approved page map; we cannot create them without source evidence.  
- Dynamic search results beyond the sampled queries are not verified; we therefore implement only static filtering on the provided inline data, not a live search API.  
- An interactive map (e.g., Google Maps) would require external scripts and network calls; we replace it with a local SVG placeholder and note the limitation.  

All other features follow the observed structure and will be built with semantic HTML5, shared CSS/JS, and vanilla JavaScript.

The shared quality-control tool ran against the site you just built and reported real failures. They are included verbatim in your task, with the file and line context where the tool gave it. Your job is the smallest set of changes that resolves them.

This is generation-stage correction. It is not the study's accessibility repair condition, and the two must not be confused: do not inject defects, do not "improve" accessibility beyond fixing what failed, and do not treat this as a second chance to redesign.

Boundaries that do not move: the approved source, the page map, the category, the model attribution, the output directory, and every other group's files. You may not weaken, edit or work around the QC tool, and you may not delete a page or a control to make a check pass. If a failure can only be fixed by changing the approved scope, say so and stop.

The orchestrator has already preserved your initial output as the study's raw artifact, so you are editing a copy. Resend each file you change in full through the file protocol — there is no patch mode, and a partial file overwrites a working one with a broken one.

Read the failures carefully before changing anything. The tool reports several distinct kinds:

- **Missing required file** — the deliverable is incomplete; add it.
- **Broken link or asset** — the target does not exist at that relative path. Fix the path or create the target; do not delete the link.
- **`href="#"` placeholder** — give the control a real destination or make it a labelled demo control.
- **Root-absolute path** — starts with `/` and breaks `file://`; make it relative.
- **Remote dependency or network request** — something is loaded over the network; inline it or replace it with a local asset.
- **Missing landmark, skip link, `lang` or instrumentation** — add it to every page the tool names, not only the first.
- **`axe` violation** — the rule ID names the WCAG failure and the node is given; fix the markup rather than suppressing the rule.
- **Horizontal scroll at 375px** — something has a fixed width or overflows; make it reflow.
- **JS or console error** — a real runtime error on that page; fix the script.
- **Invalid JSON** — a documentation artifact is malformed; re-emit it valid.

A failure you cannot reproduce from the evidence is still a failure: the tool ran, you did not. Ask for the detail you need in your notes instead of guessing.

When you have resent every change, emit `=== STATUS: COMPLETE ===` with a list of what you changed and why, plus anything you could not fix and the reason. Update `fidelity-notes.md` if a correction changed how the replica relates to its reference, and leave the `validation_summary` gates in `generation-metadata.json` alone — the orchestrator sets them from the re-run, and you have still not run anything yourself. The orchestrator re-runs QC and keeps both reports.


## The file protocol

Emit every file between sentinel lines, exactly like this:

=== FILE: index.html ===
<!doctype html>
...complete file contents...
=== END FILE ===

Rules for the protocol:
- One sentinel pair per file. Never nest them and never put two files in one block.
- Always write the file's COMPLETE contents. There is no patch or diff mode, and "..." or
  "unchanged" placeholders are rejected. Re-emitting a path replaces that file.
- Paths are relative to the site root and lowercase, except README.md, and limited to the site root or
  css/, js/, assets/ and data/. Allowed extensions: .html .css .js .svg .json .md .txt
- Markdown code fences inside a block are optional and are stripped if present.
- End every reply with one status line:
    === STATUS: CONTINUE ===   more files still to come, you will be asked to go on
    === STATUS: COMPLETE ===   the deliverable is finished
- If a reply would be cut off, stop at a file boundary, emit CONTINUE, and finish in the next reply.
- Prose outside the blocks is kept as your notes; keep it short.
